clips.title: The story
paras: Training the Beast is the culminating rite of passage for young tauren hunters in Mulgore. After demonstrating the spiritual patience and resolve required to soothe the wild beasts of the plains, hunters are sent to Thunder Bluff to learn the lifelong discipline of bonding with, nourishing, and commanding a permanent animal companion.

Having successfully tested their spirit against the dangerous predators of Mulgore—plainstriders, prairie stalkers, and swoops—tauren hunters are judged ready for the true mantle of the hunter. Yaw Sharpmane, the mentor in Bloodhoof Village, entrusts the novice with a journey to Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. There stands Holt Thunderhorn, a legendary figure among the shu'halo whose reputation for communing with the wilds is surpassed only by his reverence for the Earthmother.

To the tauren, a beast is not a simple weapon or thrall; it is a partner granted through harmony with the natural world. Holt Thunderhorn imparts the vital knowledge required to sustain this partnership. A hunter must learn not only how to guide the creature's combat instincts, but how to nourish its body through regular feeding, mend its injuries, and call its spirit back should it fall defending its companion on the plains.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: You now have the power to tame a pet, but you must also gain the skills to train it.
Travel to Thunder Bluff. There you must speak to one of our most revered hunters, Holt Thunderhorn. If he deems you worthy, he will give you the ability to train your new pet.

Holt has bested the most powerful and feared beasts of Azeroth, and commands many strong creatures of his own. His ties to the Earthmother are strong, and you can learn much from him. Good luck, friend.

clips.title: Completion
paras: A young adventurer, I see. Yes, I can bestow you with the skills you need to train and guide your pet. Not only will you be able to teach your pet new abilities, you will now be able to feed your pet, as well as revive it, should it fall in battle.
Now, go forth. May the Earthmother guide you on your path. We shall speak again, at a later date.
